newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: African presidents in Bangui for peace signing.
newsitem.headline: African presidents in Bangui for peace signing.

text.p: Preisdents Omar Bongo of Gabon and Idriss Deby of Chad arrived in Central African Republic on Saturday for the formal signing multi-party deal to seal peace after a fresh army revolt and ethnic killings, officials said.

Bongo and Deby, who launched peace talks in December with the presidents of Mali and Burkina Faso, were to hold talks with their mediating team, President Ange-Felix Patasse and other political players before the signing later in the day.
Mutinous soldiers and mediators signed an accord on Friday formally ending their revolt, which began on November 15 and was the third in under a year.

The peace deal envisages a government of national unity, amnesties and African peacekeepers replacing troops from former colonial power France, who have been acting as a buffer between the mutineers and bitter rivals in the presidential guard.
The timing of the arrival of the peacekeepers was not immediately clear.
The four presidents launched the mediation bid in December at the behest of a Franco-African summit in Burkina Faso. Mali's respected former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, brokered the deal.
Mutinies in April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian politician who won presidential elections in 1993.
The latest mutiny degenerated into ethnic feuding. The mutineers were from the minority Yakoma tribe of former military leader Andre Kolingba. The overall death toll ran into hundreds.
